messages:
Lee: Quick RFC follow-up: do we standardize on brokered short-lived claims or keep resource-scoped long-lived keys for service auth?
Ana: TL;DR: broker gives revocation + least-privilege; long-lived keys give offline/cron simplicity.
Tom: Hybrid proposal: issue opaque handle (hh_*) that clients keep. To call APIs you exchange handle -> short-lived claim (30-120s). SDKs auto-exchange & cache.
Priya (SRE): Ops: broker outage fallback must be defined. Suggest fallback to read-only long-lived keys and feature-flag per-tenant. Also need revoke propagation via pub/sub.
Lee: Security: require PoP or HMAC proof on exchange to prevent handle misuse. Store handle secret in KMS; broker validates HMAC.
Ana: Perf: add local cache keyed by (handle, resource) with small TTL to avoid cold-start thundering herds. Singleflight exchange to dedupe concurrent requests.
Tom: Migration: phase 1 internal services, phase 2 SDK/CLI customers opt-in, phase 3 deprecate legacy admin keys after 90 days. Canary on Dedicated.
Priya (SRE): Metrics: exchange_count, latency P50/P95, cache_hit_ratio, failed_hmacs, revoked_handles. Alert on spikes.
security-bot: Action created: RFC delta + security checklist + perf test plan.
Lee: I'll draft delta today. Decision by EOW? :rocket:
